chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding a man who pays his zakat, distributes part of it, and the remainder remains while he seeks the recipients for it, and there is a period of three months between the beginning and the end of this distribution, he said: 'There is no objection (to this delay).'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to delay distributing zakat for several months after taking it from one's wealth?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the delay in distributing zakat is permissible even if it spans three months, provided the distribution is eventually completed. This ruling reflects the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the timing of zakat disbursement, distinguishing between the obligation to pay and the specific deadline for distribution among the eight categories mentioned in the Quran.
